findings.evidence: The row maps an "object with no `properties`" to `Record<string, unknown>` without accounting for `required`. For `{type: object, required: [id]}`, that emitted type accepts `{}`, although the schema requires an `id` key.
findings.fix: Honor required names even when they have no entry in properties. For this example emit `{ id: unknown; [key: string]: unknown }`; when additionalProperties has a schema, use its value type for those required keys. Add an eval checking that an absent required key is rejected.

findings.evidence: The worked report says "no `Approximate` types", but the displayed User interface has no index signature even though additionalProperties defaults to true. A fresh response literal `{ id: "u", email: "e", extra: 1 }` is valid under that response schema but fails assignment to the displayed User interface because of TypeScript excess-property checking.
findings.fix: For objects with fixed properties and additionalProperties absent, true or {}, include `[key: string]: unknown` to preserve their open shape. Alternatively, explicitly mark the compact interface Approximate and propagate that status into its containers and report. Add a positive eval using a fresh object literal with an additional key.

findings.evidence: The naming rule says to add a media suffix "only when one status has several media types with different schemas". Following that rule for application/json and application/xml referencing the same object schema omits the suffix, although the bodies-and-responses rule emits an object type for JSON and string for XML.
findings.fix: Compare the effective emitted wire types after media handling, not merely the source schemas. Use media-specific names whenever those emitted types differ, for example GetReportResponse200Json and GetReportResponse200Xml even when both media entries reference the same schema.
